newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria swears in local officials after polls.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria swears in local officials after polls.

text.p: Military-ruled Nigeria on Monday swore into office councillors and chairmen of town halls elected about a week ago, officials said.

The ceremony, performed by state military administrators in most of the 774 local government councils, effectively marked the restoration of democracy at the lowest tier of authority in the politically-troubled West African nation.

"You have come out victorious through the people's votes... The confidence reposed in you must be used to serve the people in your constituencies and not your parties," Colonel Mohammed Marwa, Lagos state military administrator, said at a ceremony in the commercial capital Lagos.
Nigeria's military government has been under pressure to restore democracy since June 1993 when a presidential election that would have ended army rule was scrapped.

General Sani Abacha, who siezed power in the turmoil that ensued, has pledged to hand over next year but his critics doubt that he will and cite the continued detention of Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of the annulled vote, who has been detained since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president.
"We reiterate that Abacha's transition plan is a hog-wash... which he is using to perpetuate himself in power," said Ayo Obe, president of the leading rights group Civil Liberties Organisation.
Others also criticised the process, saying that some opposition politicians were barred from taking part in the polls and accusing the authorities of rigging the vote.

"The military government is beating its chest over nothing on the local council elections. Our officers who monitored the elections nationwide discovered there was a lot of rigging by party agents, including that many people voted more than once," said Clement Nwankwo, executive president of the human rights group Constitutional Rights Project.

"Others seen as belonging to the opposition were even barred from the entire exercise. I strongly believe in subsequent elections things will be worse. That is why I still maintain, like many others, that the transition plan is a sham," he said.

The local council poll is the first in a series of polls that will lead to the election of state legislators and governors later this year followed by voting for national assembly members and a civilian president next year.
The results of the council polls showed overwhelming victory for two political parties who want to adopt Abacha as their candidate for the civilian-rule presidential elections.
These are the United Nigeria Congress Party (UNCP) and the Democratic Party of Nigeria (DPN).

In all there are five registered political parties and the other three performed badly even in the home turfs of their leaders, causing official newspapers to speculate that a new leadership was emerging in the multi-ethnic nation.
It is widely expected that there will be a re-alignment of political forces across the vast nation, with many politicians moving to the winning side.

The victory of the UNCP and the DPN, who have both declared that they are prepared to pick Abacha as their candidate for the presidential election programmed for by September 1998, is also fuelling the speculation that he will stand in the election.
